coverage_exempt.reason: The original allocation-null arm sets EDI to zero at 0x45de1e, then unconditionally dereferences [EDI] at 0x45de23; it cannot complete within this family normal-return contract. All surrounding allocation-success and cleanup paths remain required; no null allocation is treated as game success.

equivalent_mutants.reason: Every Flags::sub call supplies width 32. This mutation changes only the unselected non-32-bit ternary arm, so it cannot change any invocation.

Original 0x45b137 saves EDI; its only later consumption is the terminal restore at 0x45b231. No pointer to this saved word escapes and the restored native local is not an exported result under the ordinary ABI.

The return-address word for original call 0x45c376 to 0x45c7c0 is not read by the callee or its normal callees. Only incoming arguments and local aliases are consumed. Ordinary canonical return uses C++ control flow; return-PC inspection is outside this contract.

The return-address word for original call 0x45c510 to 0x45c3d0 is never inspected or passed by address. The callee consumes its three arguments and returns normally at 0x45c419. The ordinary contract has no return-PC channel.

Original call 0x45cc8e to 0x45f490 uses a local output alias and incoming arguments, never its entry return word. The return at 0x45f4f9 is ordinary C++ control flow in the translation; deleting this unobserved return-PC store changes no permitted output.

Original call 0x45d268 to 0x42b9c0 reads incoming words at entry+4 and entry+8, publishes application fields and posts a message, but never reads or exposes entry+0. The ordinary canonical ABI does not observe the stored return PC.

At original 0x45df69 this mutation moves the SEH state store from entry-4 to entry+0. On this failure-return continuation the CString destructor receives entry-0x58, and the epilogue reads the saved FS head at entry-0xc and register saves, not either changed word. Equivalent only for the declared ordinary normal-return contract, which excludes guest exception unwinds and return-PC inspection.

At the call corresponding to original 0x45e12e, the shifted argument read selects the saved EDI word at entry-0xc instead of the explicitly pushed zero. This canonical body initializes EDI to zero and saves it unconditionally; no intervening call or store touches that saved word. Both reads therefore yield zero for every permitted invocation.

Original 0x45e3a1 writes a temporary address to entry-4. Normal CString work uses ECX directly; subsequent temporary preparations overwrite this scratch word. Its final restore into ECX is terminal and ECX is not an exported result. No guest exception transport is claimed.
Original 0x45e7c0 saves ESI; only terminal restores at 0x45e86f or 0x45e874 consume this word. It is not passed by address and the restored native local is not observable through the ordinary ABI.

Original 0x45e9a8 saves EBX; live loop state uses separate locals. Its only read is the terminal restore at 0x45ea6e followed by stack cleanup and return. No permitted normal-return output depends on the saved value.

Original 0x45f104 saves ESI, read only by terminal restores. The owned code clamps music to 0..100 at 0x45f22e..0x45f23e and sound to 0..80 at 0x45f2e1..0x45f2f1. The hash-verified sound multiplier at 0x50e8b0 is negative 0.125, so subtraction of the converted negative index accesses initialized table slots, never the saved ESI word. This conclusion follows from owned clamps, not a restriction to selected test inputs.

At original 0x45f434 the force=1 argument is irrelevant on this callsite: 0x45f42e/0x45f430 invoke 0x429ed0 only when the new clamped scale differs from application+0x68. The callee repeats that comparison at 0x429ef1/0x429ef4, bypasses its sole initial force read at 0x429ef6, and overwrites the argument slot at 0x429f23 before any callback. All other arguments and effects are retained.
